claims.text: Increasing atomic size mismatch in AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA coatings increases local lattice distortion.
Greater local lattice distortion enhances wear resistance by impeding dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion delays plastic deformation and reduces shear-band and microcrack formation.
Mn is smaller and Cu is larger than Cr for purposes of tuning atomic size mismatch by Cr substitution.
Partial substitution of Cr with Mn or Cu can vary calculated atomic size mismatch from approximately 2% to 8%.
XRD line broadening can be used as a measurement of local lattice distortion in these coatings.
TEM dislocation-density measurements characterize the proposed local-lattice-distortion mediator.
XRD phase identification and EDS chemical mapping can reveal unintended phase changes or chemical heterogeneity.
Higher atomic size mismatch impedes dislocation nucleation during wear.
Higher atomic size mismatch impedes dislocation mobility during wear.
Delaying plastic deformation reduces shear-band formation and microcrack propagation that degrade wear performance.
Samples with increased atomic size mismatch will have lower wear rates than the baseline composition.
Samples with increased atomic size mismatch will have higher hardness than the baseline composition.
Samples with increased atomic size mismatch will have shallower plastic-deformation zones than the baseline composition.
The predicted relationship will hold over an atomic-size-mismatch range of approximately 2% to 8% if phase and chemical changes are absent.
The baseline AlCoCrFeNi composition has minimal atomic size mismatch.
The proposed effect may not extend to conditions that induce significant phase changes or chemical segregation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says overall stoichiometry or composition will remain constant, while the intervention intentionally replaces part of Cr with Mn or Cu. Elemental stoichiometry necessarily changes under such substitution unless 'constant' is restricted to total atomic fraction or another explicitly defined quantity.

Local lattice distortion is presented as being measured through both XRD line broadening and TEM dislocation density, but dislocation density is a distinct defect metric rather than a direct measure of atomic-size-induced static lattice distortion. The mediator and its operational measurement are therefore not consistently defined.
